title: Refit and lock a table saw's riving knife after dado work
instruction: The dado set has just come off the saw and its blade is back on. Fit the riving knife back on behind the blade and lock it in place.
context: Ripping boards on a table saw is core carpentry (O*NET 47-2031.00 Carpenters: cut materials "using hand tools, machines, or power saws"), and putting blades and attachments on saws is a listed task of saw setters (51-7041.00). The riving knife, the steel plate just behind the blade, stops kickback. SawStop's manual says it "may not be used" with a dado set (p. 33), so when the blade goes back on after dado work the knife must be refitted before the next rip (OSHA 1910.213(c)(2)): required setup, not an aside. The difficulty is physical: a 2.3 mm plate goes down onto 6 mm pins with 0.5 mm of play, in a 14 cm opening a few cm from the teeth, and stays seated while an over-centre clamp handle is pushed through its resistance to the click, whose snap pushes the knife across its pins. The rules don't say which arm does what. No task on the board sets up a saw's safety hardware.
setup: Station table, fixed layout (object_jitter=0); cm, x away from the robot, y to its left, z up from the floor. The top of a 10 in cabinet table saw (SawStop's Professional Cabinet Saw sizes), unplugged, set into a cutout in the bench: its cast-iron top (485 x 485 mm of the real 20 x 27 in top, 2 cm thick, x 10.5 to 59, y -26.25 to 22.25) is 9.5 cm above the bench, at 84.25 cm; sheet-steel cabinet walls (1 cm) below it. The blade (10 in: 254 mm at its tips; a 2 mm plate with 40 carbide tips 3 mm wide, the kerf, turned to face out with their corners on its rim) runs along y in the plane x 25, its arbor at y -2, z 79.49, raised fully: 3-1/8 in (79.4 mm) above the top. The table insert is out; the opening (modelled, 140 x 340 mm) is x 15.5 to 29.5, y -22.5 to 11.5. Under it, behind the blade (toward -y), the knife mount: a steel base plate (1 cm thick, its face at x 25.115, y -22.2 to -15.2, z 77.55 to 82.05) with two steel locating pins 6 mm across, 2 mm long, at y -16.4 and -18.7, z 78.99; and a red steel clamp lever (0.25 kg) on a hinge along y through x 23.39, z 80.34: a 10 x 10 mm shaft from y -21.2 to 7.2 (it brings the handle forward, in front of the blade: modelled), a pressure plate whose 2 mm face (y -20.9 to -16.4) sits 1.5 to 3.5 mm below the hinge and 15 mm in front of it, a handle arm at y 4.8 to 7.2 ending in a 20 x 24 x 8 mm pad 50 mm toward the robot from the hinge, and a 20 mm spring arm. The over-centre spring (60.5 N/mm along a line 0.3 rad from vertical, toward the robot) runs from a steel seat (8 x 8 x 6 mm, its top at x 22.44, y 6, z 77.28) to the spring arm. Handle up (its pad's top 6 mm below the saw top, the plate 3.5 mm back from the knife's place): held up by 0.1 N m. Pushed down, it resists (up to 8 N at the pad) until its dead centre, 19.5 mm down (70% of the way), then snaps down and presses the plate on the knife with at least 100 N. With no knife it goes on to a stop 0.85 rad down, the plate 1.9 mm off the base plate. The riving knife: 2.3 mm steel plate, 0.133 kg, 140 x 140 mm; its front edge 5 mm from the blade, its top 3 mm below the teeth, its foot with two open slots 7 mm wide, 14 mm deep, placed so that unheld it stands on its pins (its centre of mass 6 mm behind the front one). It stands upright in a wooden holder on the bench right of the saw, as it goes on the saw (the knife spans y -42 to -28; the holder y -42.4 to -34.7): two blocks 1.7 x 6.2 x 2.5 cm each side of a 3 mm slot, and a 1.2 x 0.8 x 6.4 cm post under its lower front edge. Home: both slots' ends on the pins, flat on the base plate. All objects: rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), except the knife's slotted foot: steel on steel, 0.35 static, 0.30 dynamic.
scoring: Scored at the end; a full score must hold for 1 s. 0 if the knife ends off the bench (its outline's centre below the bench top or off the table), the arms' state can't be read, the knife, lever, blade or a pin isn't the shape built here (reported outlines within 0.5 mm; the lever centred on its hinge; the blade and pins lying along x), or the simulator reports a non-finite number or a non-unit orientation, or the knife's or the lever's state is missing or unreadable, or the knife or a gripper moves more than 40 cm in one step (8 m/s: a reset the file didn't see, or a broken reading) (those void the trial). Otherwise: 1.0 if locked, every gripper's tool point at least 3 cm, and a 3 x 3 grid of points over each finger pad at least 1 cm, from the knife's and the lever's outlines, and both still (each moved under 0.5 mm and 0.025 rad since the last step, i.e. 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s, judged from their poses), held for 1 s (20 steps); 0.75 if locked: seated, flat on the base plate (a 0.4 mm feeler gauge won't go between them), turned less than 1 degree, and the handle down past its dead centre with the pressure plate on the knife (the same 0.4 mm gauge won't go between them; it may press a little into the knife, as simulated contacts give); 0.5 if seated: both slots' ends on their pins (the knife's frame within 1 mm of home along y and up), over the pins' 2 mm length, turned less than 3 degrees; 0.25 if both pins are in the slots but it isn't down: within 1 mm of home along y, at most 8 mm above home, over the pins, turned less than 5 degrees. Capped at 0.5 if, at any one step or anywhere on the way since the last one (each point moving in a straight line), a gripper's tool point or any point of its finger pads' faces (30 x 27 mm) came within 5 mm of the blade's tooth band (its outer 8 mm out to the tips, 3 mm thick), or any point of the knife's boxes within 2 mm of it: carbide tips chip when struck. These distances are computed from the shapes at each step, to within 0.1 mm and never as further than they are, and checked every 2 mm of travel between steps. Positions are of the knife's own frame (the centre of its slotted foot plate).
reset_notes: Fixed layout. Each reset stands the knife back in its holder and puts the clamp handle up; nothing is consumed. For a real trial: unplug the saw, raise the blade fully, take out the table insert, lift the clamp handle, take out the knife and stand it in its holder.
fidelity: Only the saw's top 9.5 cm and the knife mount are modelled; the top sits in a bench cutout at 84 cm (the real top is about 86 cm up). The knife is 2.3 mm plate built from boxes. The real handle turns a cam that pushes a separate pressure plate; here a 2 mm plate face just below the hinge acts like that cam near its high point, and the over-centre spring is a PhysX D6 joint with one linear drive. Clamp force at least 100 N (not published). The blade doesn't turn; the insert stays out.
